lessons.title: Goal Seek
learn: Sales needed for a profit target
lessons.mac:
Data > What-If Analysis > Goal Seek
Same three boxes: Set cell, To value, By changing cell
Works in Excel for Mac, Windows and the web

steps.say: Your manager asks two questions. How many units must the Pune showroom sell to make five lakh rupees profit a month? And how big a home loan can you take if the EMI must stay at thirty thousand? Goal Seek answers both in seconds, without any algebra.
You will learn what Goal Seek needs, how to use it for a profit target, and how to work backwards from an EMI to a loan amount. The practice sheet is S14-01.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. The three boxes of Goal Seek
2. Units needed for a profit target
3. The loan you can afford for a given EMI

Practice: sheet S14-01

steps.say: Goal Seek works backwards. You tell it which formula cell to watch, the value you want it to show, and which single input it may change. It then tries values until the formula hits your target.

acts.t:
Goal Seek: three boxes

Set cell: the formula cell you care about (Profit, EMI)
To value: the number you want it to show
By changing cell: one input cell Goal Seek may change

Data > What-If Analysis > Goal Seek

steps.say: Here is the model. Price is twelve hundred and fifty rupees, variable cost seven hundred and eighty, fixed costs six lakh a month. At two thousand units in B4, profit in B8 is three lakh forty thousand rupees.
With B8 selected, go to the Data tab, click What-If Analysis and choose Goal Seek.
Set cell is B8, the profit. To value, five lakh, typed as five followed by five zeros. By changing cell is B4, units sold. Click OK.

Goal Seek found a solution. B4 now shows two thousand three hundred and forty units, and profit is five lakh. You can't sell part of a unit, so the real answer is two thousand three hundred and forty-one. Click OK to keep the result.

Now the loan. At twenty-five lakh, eight point seven five percent, for two hundred and forty months, the EMI in B14 is twenty-two thousand and ninety-three rupees. We want the loan that gives exactly thirty thousand.

Here is the most common mistake. Open Goal Seek and put the loan amount, B11, in the Set cell box. Click OK, and Excel complains that the cell must contain a formula. Set cell is always the result, never the input.
Fix it. Set cell is B14, the EMI formula. To value, thirty thousand. By changing cell, B11, the loan amount. Click OK, then OK again.
You can borrow about thirty-three lakh ninety-four thousand rupees and keep the EMI at thirty thousand. That is a number worth knowing before you visit the bank.

Pro tip: Goal Seek overwrites the input cell. If you want the original back, press Command Z straight away. Goal Seek also changes only one input; when several inputs and limits are involved, use Solver.

acts.t:
Pro tip

• Goal Seek overwrites the input: ⌘ + Z to undo
• One input only. Several inputs or limits → Solver (lesson S14-04)
• Want a whole number? Round up yourself: 2,340.4 units → 2,341

steps.say: On a Mac, Goal Seek is in the same place: Data tab, What-If Analysis, Goal Seek. The dialog has the same three boxes, so everything you saw here works the same way.

acts.t:
Mac corner

Data > What-If Analysis > Goal Seek
Same three boxes: Set cell, To value, By changing cell
Works in Excel for Mac, Windows and the web

steps.say: To recap: Set cell is the formula, To value is your target, By changing cell is the one input. Use it for sales targets, EMIs and break-even questions.

acts.t:
Recap

• Set cell = formula, To value = target, By changing = one input
• Profit target → units needed
• EMI target → affordable loan

steps.say: Your challenge: put units back to two thousand, then find the selling price that still gives five lakh profit. The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

Type 2000 in B4. Use Goal Seek to find the selling price (B2) that gives a profit of ₹5,00,000.

Answer: sheet S14-01 Done, cell D4

lessons.title: Scenario Manager
lessons.mac:
• Data > What-If Analysis > Scenario Manager
• Name your input cells first (Name Box) so the summary is readable
• Not available in Excel for the web; use the Mac app
• Scenarios travel with the .xlsx file

steps.say: Budget meetings always ask for three versions: what if things go well, as planned, or badly. Scenario Manager stores each version of your inputs under a name and builds a one-page summary comparing them.

acts.t:
Finished result

• Three saved scenarios on sheet S14-02: Base, Best, Worst
• A Scenario Summary sheet comparing Revenue and Net profit:
   Base ₹2,18,49,600 · Best ₹2,98,94,400 · Worst ₹1,23,74,400
• Show any scenario with one click

steps.say: You will learn to add scenarios, show them on the model, fix a typical entry mistake, and create the summary report. The practice sheet is S14-02. This lesson is recorded in Excel desktop, and the Mac path is the same.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. Add Base, Best and Worst scenarios
2. Show a scenario on the model
3. Scenario Summary report

Practice: sheet S14-02 · Mac: Data > What-If Analysis > Scenario Manager

steps.say: A scenario is just a saved set of values for a few input cells. Scenario Manager can swap them into the model, and its summary lists the result cells for every scenario side by side.

acts.t:
Scenario Manager

Changing cells: the inputs (here B4:B6: growth, price change, cost inflation)
Scenario: a named set of values for those cells
Show: puts a scenario's values into the model
Summary: a new sheet comparing result cells (B16 Revenue, B19 Net profit)

steps.say: Here is the plan for financial year twenty-six twenty-seven. Inputs are in B4 to B6, and they have names: Growth, Price Change and Cost Inflation. At ten percent growth, net profit in B19 is two crore eighteen lakh rupees.
On the Data tab, click What-If Analysis, then Scenario Manager. Click Add. Name the first scenario Base, set Changing cells to B4 colon B6, and click OK.
The Scenario Values box shows today's numbers, ten, three and six percent, as decimals. They are the base case, so just click OK.
Click Add again for Best. Same changing cells. Now watch a mistake many people make: typing eighteen for eighteen percent. Enter eighteen, five and four, and click OK.
Select Best and click Show. Growth jumps to eighteen hundred percent and the profit is absurd. The box takes plain numbers, so eighteen percent must be typed as zero point one eight.
To fix it, keep Best selected and click Edit. Click OK on the cells, then type zero point one eight, zero point zero five and zero point zero four, and click OK.
Add the Worst case the same way: zero point zero two growth, zero price change and zero point zero nine cost inflation.
Select Best and click Show. Net profit rises to about two crore ninety-nine lakh. Select Worst and click Show. It falls to about one crore twenty-four lakh.
Now the report. Click Summary. Choose Scenario summary, and in Result cells type B16 comma B19, for revenue and net profit. Click OK.

Excel adds a sheet called Scenario Summary. Because we named the cells, rows read Growth and Net Profit instead of cell addresses. It is a static report, so create it again after you change a scenario.
Back on sheet S14-02, open Scenario Manager, select Base, click Show and then Close, so the model is back to the plan.

On a Mac, Scenario Manager is under Data, What-If Analysis, exactly as here. Excel for the web can't create scenarios, so build them in the Mac app. Scenarios are saved inside the file and open fine on Windows.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• Data > What-If Analysis > Scenario Manager
• Name your input cells first (Name Box) so the summary is readable
• Not available in Excel for the web; use the Mac app
• Scenarios travel with the .xlsx file

steps.say: To recap: a scenario is a named set of input values. Type percentages as decimals. The summary report compares every scenario on one sheet.

acts.t:
Recap

• Add one scenario per case, same changing cells
• Percentages as decimals: 0.18, not 18
• Summary with result cells = one-page comparison

steps.say: Your challenge: add a Festive scenario with twenty-five percent growth, two percent price change and eight percent cost inflation, then rebuild the summary. The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

Add scenario Festive: Growth 0.25, PriceChange 0.02, CostInflation 0.08.
Rebuild the summary. What are Revenue and Net profit?

Answer: sheet S14-02 Done, row 13

lessons.title: Data Tables
learn: Sensitivity of profit to price and volume
lessons.mac:
• Data > What-If Analysis > Data Table
• Same Row input cell / Column input cell boxes
• Excel for the web cannot create Data Tables

steps.say: When a customer asks what the EMI would be at nine percent over fifteen years, or ten percent over twenty-five, you don't want to retype the formula each time. A Data Table shows every combination of rate and tenure in one grid.

acts.t:
Finished result

• Sheet S14-03: a grid of EMIs for a ₹30,00,000 loan
• Rates 7.5% to 10.5% down the side, tenures 10 to 30 years across
• 8.5% for 20 years = ₹26,035, the same as the model in B5
• Change the loan amount and every EMI updates

steps.say: You will learn how a two-variable Data Table is laid out, how to choose the row and column input cells, and how to avoid swapping them. Practice sheet S14-03, recorded in Excel desktop; the Mac menu is the same.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. Layout: formula in the top-left corner
2. Row input cell and Column input cell
3. The swapped-inputs mistake

Practice: sheet S14-03 · Mac: Data > What-If Analysis > Data Table

steps.say: A Data Table needs one formula in the top-left corner, values to try across the top, and values to try down the side. Row input cell is the model cell that the top row replaces. Column input cell is the one the side column replaces.

acts.t:
Two-variable Data Table

Top-left corner: =B5 (the result you want)
Top row: tenures to try → Row input cell = B4 (tenure)
Left column: rates to try → Column input cell = B3 (rate)

Excel fills the grid with {=TABLE(B4,B3)}

steps.say: The model is at the top. Thirty lakh rupees at eight and a half percent for twenty years gives an EMI of twenty-six thousand and thirty-five rupees in B5.
The grid is ready below: tenures in B8 to F8, rates in A9 to A15. In the corner cell A8, type equals B5 and press Return. The corner must point at the result.
Select A8 to F15. On the Data tab, open What-If Analysis and choose Data Table.
First, the common mistake. Put B3, the rate, in Row input cell and B4, the tenure, in Column input cell, and click OK. The numbers make no sense, because Excel is plugging years in as interest rates.
Press Command Z to undo. Remember: the top row holds tenures, so Row input cell is B4. The left column holds rates, so Column input cell is B3.
Select A8 to F15 again, open Data Table, type B4 for Row input cell and B3 for Column input cell, and click OK.

Check one cell against the model. D11 is eight and a half percent for twenty years: twenty-six thousand and thirty-five rupees, the same as B5. At ten and a half percent for ten years, B15 shows forty thousand four hundred and eighty.
It is live. Change the loan in B2 to forty lakh and every EMI in the grid updates. Then set it back to thirty lakh.

Pro tip: you can't edit one cell inside the grid; Excel says you can't change part of a data table. To remove it, select the whole results area and press Delete. Big tables can slow a workbook, so you can set calculation to Automatic except for data tables.

acts.t:
Pro tip

• Edit or delete the whole results area, never one cell
• Slow file? Mac: Excel > Preferences > Calculation > Automatic except for data tables
  (Windows: Formulas > Calculation Options)
• Press F9 (fn + F9 on a MacBook) to recalculate

steps.say: On a Mac, it is Data, What-If Analysis, Data Table, with the same two boxes. Excel for the web shows existing data tables but can't create one, so build them in the Mac app.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• Data > What-If Analysis > Data Table
• Same Row input cell / Column input cell boxes
• Excel for the web cannot create Data Tables

steps.say: To recap: put the result formula in the corner. Row input cell matches the values across the top; Column input cell matches the values down the side. Check one cell against the model.

acts.t:
Recap

• Corner cell = the result formula
• Row input = across, Column input = down
• Verify one cell against the model

steps.say: Your challenge is below the EMI grid. Build a profit table for prices across the top and units down the side, starting at A25. The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

In A25 type =B23. Select A25:F30 > Data Table.
Row input cell B19 (price), Column input cell B20 (units).
What profit do you get at ₹1,350 and 2,400 units?

Answer: sheet S14-03 Done, cell F30

lessons.title: Solver
lessons.mac:
• Tools > Excel Add-ins > Solver Add-in, then Data > Solver
• Same dialog, same three methods
• Reports (Answer, Sensitivity) appear as new sheets
• Excel for the web: different add-in; use the Mac app

steps.say: An electronics store has forty-six lakh forty thousand rupees to stock up for Diwali, a thousand square feet of warehouse, and a demand limit on each product. Solver found the mix that earns the most: a hundred TVs and seventy ACs, for six lakh forty-two thousand rupees profit.

You will learn how to switch Solver on, how to describe a problem with an objective, variable cells and constraints, and how to read the answer. Practice sheet S14-04, recorded in Excel desktop with the Mac menus shown.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. Turn on the Solver add-in
2. Objective, variable cells, constraints
3. Solve, read the result, avoid the negative-units trap

Practice: sheet S14-04

steps.say: Solver is Goal Seek with many inputs and rules. The objective is the cell to maximise or minimise. Variable cells are what Solver may change. Constraints are the limits. Simplex LP is the method for straight-line models like this one.

acts.t:
Solver in plain English

Objective: H6 total profit → Max
Variable cells: F2:F5 units to stock
Constraints: G6 ≤ B8 (budget), I6 ≤ B9 (space), F2:F5 ≤ E2:E5 (demand), F2:F5 = integer
Method: Simplex LP (linear), GRG Nonlinear (curves), Evolutionary (messy models)

steps.say: First, switch Solver on. On a Mac, open the Tools menu, choose Excel Add-ins, tick Solver Add-in and click OK. On Windows it is File, Options, Add-ins. A Solver button then appears on the right of the Data tab.

acts.t:
Turn on Solver (once)

Mac: Tools > Excel Add-ins > tick Solver Add-in > OK
Windows: File > Options > Add-ins > Excel Add-ins > Go > tick Solver Add-in

Then: Data tab > Solver (far right)

steps.say: Here is the model. Units to stock in F2 to F5 are all zero. Columns G, H and I multiply them by cost, profit and space, and row 6 adds them up. The budget is in B8 and the space limit in B9.
On the Data tab, click Solver. Set Objective to H6 and choose Max. In By Changing Variable Cells, type F2 colon F5.

acts.h: Set By Changing Variable Cells to $F$2:$F$5

steps.say: Click Add for the first constraint. Cell Reference G6, less than or equal to, B8: total cost within budget. Click Add to save it and start the next one.
I6 less than or equal to B9, for space. Click Add. Then F2 to F5 less than or equal to E2 to E5, so we never stock more than demand. Click Add.
Last, whole units only. Cell Reference F2 to F5, and choose int from the list. Click OK to go back to the main window.

Now the common trap. Untick Make Unconstrained Variables Non-Negative, choose Simplex LP and click Solve. Solver stocks a negative number of some products to free up budget, which is impossible in real life.

acts.h: Set Select a Solving Method to Simplex LP

steps.say: Open Solver again. Your settings are remembered. Tick Make Unconstrained Variables Non-Negative and click Solve.
Solver found a solution. Keep Solver Solution is selected. Also tick Answer under Reports, then click OK.

Excel added an Answer Report sheet. It lists each constraint as Binding or Not Binding. The budget is binding: every rupee is used. Space is not: we use eight hundred and ninety of a thousand square feet.

Back on S14-04: a hundred TVs and seventy ACs, total cost forty-six lakh forty thousand, profit six lakh forty-two thousand rupees. No fridges or washing machines, because they earn less per rupee of budget.

On a Mac, Solver lives on the Data tab once the add-in is ticked in Tools, Excel Add-ins. The dialog is the same. Excel for the web uses a different Solver add-in, so build Solver models in the Mac app.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• Tools > Excel Add-ins > Solver Add-in, then Data > Solver
• Same dialog, same three methods
• Reports (Answer, Sensitivity) appear as new sheets
• Excel for the web: different add-in; use the Mac app

steps.say: To recap: describe the goal, the cells Solver may change, and every real-world limit. Always tick Non-Negative, and read the Answer Report to see which limit is holding you back.

acts.t:
Recap

• Objective + variable cells + constraints
• Tick Make Unconstrained Variables Non-Negative; Simplex LP for linear models
• Answer Report: Binding constraints are your real limits

steps.say: Your challenge: the owner can raise the budget to fifty-five lakh rupees. Change B8 and solve again. What is the new best profit, and which products change? The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

Change B8 to 5500000 and run Solver again.
What is the best profit now, and how many of each product?

Answer: sheet S14-04 Done, row 12

lessons.title: Forecast Sheet and trendlines
lessons.mac:
• Data > Forecast Sheet (Microsoft 365 / Excel 2019 and later)
• Dates evenly spaced, no gaps; up to 30% missing values are filled in
• Excel for the web: no button, but =FORECAST.ETS() works

steps.say: Here are forty-two months of sales with a Diwali peak every October and November, and a forecast for the next six months with a shaded range. Excel built the forecast in one click, and it already expects this year's festive spike.

You will learn to add a trendline to a chart, to create a Forecast Sheet, and to explain the confidence band to your manager in plain words. Practice sheet S14-05, recorded in Excel desktop; the Mac path is the same.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. A linear trendline on a chart
2. Data > Forecast Sheet for seasonal data
3. Confidence bands in plain English

Practice: sheet S14-05 · Mac: Data > Forecast Sheet

steps.say: A trendline draws a straight line through the past and extends it. Forecast Sheet uses a method called exponential smoothing that also learns the yearly pattern. The confidence band says: we are ninety-five percent sure the actual will land between these two lines.

acts.t:
Two ways to look ahead

Trendline: straight line, ignores seasons
Forecast Sheet: FORECAST.ETS, learns trend + seasonal pattern

95% confidence band: Excel is 95% sure the real number will fall between the lower and upper line.
Wider band = less certainty.

steps.say: The data is in two columns: the month in A, as a real date, and sales in B. Months must be evenly spaced with no gaps, or the forecast can't run.
Select A1 to B43. On the Insert tab, open the line chart button and pick Line.
With the chart selected, go to Chart Design, Add Chart Element, Trendline, Linear. The dotted line shows sales rising steadily.
This is the common mistake: using a straight line for seasonal sales. It runs right through the Diwali peaks and the quiet monsoon months, so it under-forecasts October and over-forecasts July.
Click cell A1 to leave the chart, then select A1 to B43 again. On the Data tab, click Forecast Sheet.

Set Forecast End to the first of March twenty twenty-seven, the last month of this financial year. Click Options to see the settings: confidence interval ninety-five percent, and seasonality detected automatically.
Click Create. Excel adds a new sheet with a table and a chart. The orange line is the forecast, and the thin lines are the lower and upper confidence bounds.

Scroll to the forecast rows. October and November twenty twenty-six come out highest, so Excel picked up the festive pattern. Click C44 to see the formula: FORECAST dot ETS, which you can also use on its own.

Pro tip: say it this way in a meeting. We expect about this much in November, and we are ninety-five percent confident it will be between the lower and upper figures. Plan stock for the upper figure, cash for the lower one.

acts.t:
Pro tip: how to present it

"We expect ₹X in November. We are 95% confident it will land between ₹Low and ₹High."

Plan inventory for the upper bound, cash flow for the lower bound.

steps.say: On a Mac with Microsoft 365, it is Data, Forecast Sheet, with the same Options. Excel for the web has no Forecast Sheet button, but the FORECAST dot ETS function works there.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• Data > Forecast Sheet (Microsoft 365 / Excel 2019 and later)
• Dates evenly spaced, no gaps; up to 30% missing values are filled in
• Excel for the web: no button, but =FORECAST.ETS() works

steps.say: To recap: trendlines suit steady growth. Forecast Sheet handles seasons. The confidence band shows how sure the forecast is.

acts.t:
Recap

• Trendline = straight-line view of the past
• Forecast Sheet = trend + seasonality (FORECAST.ETS)
• Confidence band = the honest range

steps.say: Your challenge: create the forecast again, but in Options set seasonality to twelve manually and confidence to eighty percent. What happens to the band? The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

Forecast Sheet > Options: Set Manually = 12, Confidence Interval = 80%.
Compare with the 95% version. What changes?

Answer: sheet S14-05 Done, row 52

lessons.title: Analysis ToolPak
lessons.mac:
• Tools > Excel Add-ins > Analysis ToolPak
• Data > Data Analysis: same 19 tools as Windows
• Not in Excel for the web
• The 'Analysis ToolPak - VBA' add-in is Windows only (not needed)

steps.say: We have sales, ad spend and dealer count for twenty-four districts of Gujarat. In a few clicks, the Analysis ToolPak gives a full statistics summary and a regression that says how much each lakh of advertising is worth.

You will learn to switch on the ToolPak, run Descriptive Statistics, run a Regression, and read the three numbers that matter. Practice sheet S14-06, recorded in Excel desktop with the Mac path shown.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. Turn on the Analysis ToolPak
2. Descriptive Statistics
3. Regression and how to read it

Practice: sheet S14-06

steps.say: Descriptive statistics summarise one column: average, middle value, spread, smallest and largest. Regression fits a line: sales equals a starting amount plus so much per lakh of ads plus so much per dealer. R square says how much of the ups and downs the line explains.

acts.t:
Plain English

Descriptive Statistics: Mean, Median, Standard Deviation, Min, Max, Count

Regression: Sales = Intercept + b1 × Ad Spend + b2 × Dealers
• Coefficient: change in sales for +1 of that input
• R Square: share of variation explained (0 to 1)
• P-value < 0.05: the effect is unlikely to be chance

steps.say: Switch it on once. On a Mac, open Tools, Excel Add-ins, tick Analysis ToolPak and click OK. On Windows, it is File, Options, Add-ins. A Data Analysis button appears on the Data tab.

acts.t:
Turn on the ToolPak (once)

Mac: Tools > Excel Add-ins > tick Analysis ToolPak > OK
Windows: File > Options > Add-ins > Excel Add-ins > Go

Then: Data tab > Data Analysis

steps.say: Our data: district in A, ad spend in lakh rupees in B, number of dealers in C, and sales in lakh rupees in D, for twenty-four districts.
On the Data tab, click Data Analysis. Choose Descriptive Statistics and click OK.

Input Range is D1 to D25, including the heading. Here is the usual mistake: leave Labels in first row unticked and click OK. Excel says the input range contains non-numeric data, because it is reading the heading as a number.
Tick Labels in first row. Choose Output Range and type F1. Tick Summary statistics, and click OK.

Average sales are about forty-nine point seven lakh per district. Compare the mean and the median: when they are close, there are no extreme districts pulling the average. The standard deviation shows the typical gap from the average.
Now the regression. Click Data Analysis, choose Regression and click OK.
Input Y Range is the sales, D1 to D25. Input X Range is ad spend and dealers together, B1 to C25. Tick Labels. Choose New Worksheet Ply, name it Regression, and click OK.
Look at three numbers. R Square is zero point nine four: ad spend and dealers explain ninety-four percent of the differences between districts. That is a strong model.

Then the coefficients. Each extra lakh of ad spend goes with about two point eight lakh more sales, and each extra dealer with about point eight seven lakh, holding the other one steady. Both p-values are tiny, so these effects are not chance.

Pro tip: the ToolPak pastes fixed values. If the data changes, run it again, or use formulas like AVERAGE and LINEST, as on the Done sheet, which update by themselves. And remember, regression shows association, not proof that ads cause sales.

acts.t:
Pro tip

• ToolPak output is static: rerun after data changes
• Live versions: =AVERAGE(), =STDEV.S(), =INDEX(LINEST(D2:D25,B2:C25,TRUE,TRUE),1,2)
• Regression shows association, not cause

steps.say: On a Mac, switch it on in Tools, Excel Add-ins, then use Data, Data Analysis. The dialogs match Windows. Excel for the web has no ToolPak, so use the Mac app.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• Tools > Excel Add-ins > Analysis ToolPak
• Data > Data Analysis: same 19 tools as Windows
• Not in Excel for the web
• The 'Analysis ToolPak - VBA' add-in is Windows only (not needed)

steps.say: To recap: switch on the ToolPak once. Tick Labels whenever your range includes headings. In a regression, read R Square, the coefficients and the p-values.

acts.t:
Recap

• Tools > Excel Add-ins > Analysis ToolPak
• Include headings + tick Labels
• Regression: R Square, coefficients, p-values

steps.say: Your challenge: run the Correlation tool on B1 to D25 with labels. Which is more closely linked to sales, ad spend or dealers? The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

Data > Data Analysis > Correlation, Input Range B1:D25, Labels in first row.
Which has the stronger link with Sales: Ad Spend or Dealers?

Answer: sheet S14-06 Done, row 28
